question: is energy stores thinned under the most advanced plaque?
message:
is energy stores thinned under the most advanced plaque?
I believe the correct answer is no.
reply:
Based on the provided histological image of an atherosclerotic artery, it appears you may have meant "vessel wall" or "tunica media" instead of "energy stores."

Looking at the image, the answer is actually **yes**.

If you compare the thickness of the vessel wall (the pinkish-purple muscular layer, known as the tunica media) on the right side of the image to the area directly underneath the largest part of the plaque (the yellowish, lipid-rich area), you can see that **the wall is significantly thinned (attenuated) under the plaque.**

This thinning is a common feature of advanced atherosclerosis, where the expanding plaque puts pressure on the underlying media and causes the loss of smooth muscle cells and elastic fibers in that area.
